title: Power Round — 2018 — ARML Power sub-problem rubric

criteria.name: Problem 1a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1a (2 pts). Statement: 4. a. Show that the binary partitions of 5 are totally ordered; i.e., if p andp′ are two diﬀerent binary partitions of 5, then either p≺p′ or p′≺p.

criteria.name: Problem 1b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1b (3 pts). Statement: b. Show that the binary partitions of 8 are not totally ordered, i.e., ﬁnd two binary partitions of 8 – call them q and q′ – such that q⊀q′ and q′⊀q.

criteria.name: Problem 1c
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1c (2 pts). Statement: 5. a. Find the smallest binary partition of n, using this partial ordering. That is, ﬁnd the binary partition p such that for all other binary partitions p′, p≺p′.

criteria.name: Problem 1d
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1d (3 pts). Statement: b. Find the largest binary partition of n, using this partial ordering. That is, ﬁnd the binary partition P such that for all other binary partitions P′, P≻P′.

criteria.name: Problem 3a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 3a (1 pt). Statement: 3. 23 46 12 1 Figure 1 Hasse diagrams can be drawn to show the ordering of partitions such as the ones from Problems 4 and 5. For convenience, rather than labeling the vertices in the Hasse diagram with the partition itself, like (8 , 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0), it is common to label the vertex with its nonzero parts only, using exponents to indicate parts within the partition with multiplicity greater than 1. For example, the partition (8 , 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) would be labeled 8, the partition (4, 2, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0) would be labeled 42 2, and the partition (2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0) would be labeled 2 214. 6. a. Draw the Hasse diagram for the binary partitions of 8. Label each vertex.

criteria.name: Problem 3b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 3b (1 pt). Statement: b. List a path through the Hasse diagram for the binary partitions of 8 that begins at the bottom vertex (that is, the vertex at Level 0) and, traveling only along edges, passes through every other vertex exactly once. Such a path is called a Hamiltonian path.

criteria.name: Problem 4a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 4a (3 pts). Statement: 4. Let S be the set of binary partitions of n. Let S1 be the set of binary partitions of n 2 . Let S2 be the set of binary partitions of n− 2. Prove that there is a bijection B (i.e., a one-to-one correspondence) from the set S to the set S1∪S2. Prove that this bijection B preserves order; that is, given that p≺p′ for binary partitions p,p′∈S, then either B(p)≺B(p′) or B(p) and B(p′) are incomparable.

criteria.name: Problem 4b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 4b (5 pts). Statement: d. Prove that for each positive integer n, the Hasse diagram of the binary partitions of n has a Hamiltonian path that begins with the vertex at Level 0.

criteria.name: Problem 7
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7 (3 pts). Statement: 7. Prove that the value of fL(n) is the number of binary partitions of n that have n−L nonzero parts.

criteria.name: Problem 8a
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 8a (2 pts). Statement: 8. Not all partitions are binary partitions. Some partitions have parts of the form 2 j− 1 where j is a nonnegative integer. Such partitions will be called s-partitions, and their parts are written in nonincreasing order. Two s-partitions of 5 are (3, 1, 1, 0, 0) and (1, 1, 1, 1, 1). a. List two partitions of 7, one that is an s-partition and one that is neither an s-partition nor a binary partition. Make sure to identify which is which.

criteria.name: Problem 8b
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 8b (3 pts). Statement: b. Prove that if n≥ 2L, the value of fL(n) is equal to the number of s-partitions of L.

criteria.name: Problem 9
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 9 (2 pts). Statement: 9. Draw the Hasse diagram for the trinary partitions of 12. Label each vertex.

criteria.name: Problem 10
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 10 (6 pts). Statement: 10. State a value of n less than 23 for which the Hasse diagram of the trinary partitions of n does not contain a Hamiltonian path. Prove your claim. (Recall that a Hamiltonian path is deﬁned in Problem 6b.)
